description: Check permissions, secrets, authentication, input validation, rate limits, logs, dependency issues, and admin access.
ownerAgentTitle: Imani Heartbeat — technology, security, risk, repository/engineering

baseline.notes: Row 69 is marked Complete in launch-rows.json and the Command Center snapshot. There is no dedicated ROW-69 security-baseline markdown in ops/fab-5. This review compares current repository controls against those seven baseline items plus the Row 182 checklist.

overallVerdict.summary: No committed live secrets and no unauthenticated admin bypass were found. Least-privilege RBAC, bcrypt-12 passwords, httpOnly JWT sessions, Google OAuth state, Stripe webhook signature verification, CRON bearer timing-safe compare, and log redaction are present. Residual HIGH gaps versus the Row 69 baseline remain: no Architect application MFA, no brute-force/IP rate limits on public auth and support APIs, no Content-Security-Policy or other security headers in next.config.ts/vercel.json, JWT role claims can stay stale for up to 30 days on middleware-gated pages, password reset does not revoke existing sessions, and npm audit reports 11 high / 1 moderate transitive vulnerabilities.

controlsPresent.control: Session JWTs signed with jose HS256; cookie bh-session is httpOnly, sameSite=lax, secure in production, path=/, TTL 30 days.
Passwords hashed with bcryptjs cost 12. Strength requires min 8 characters plus at least one letter and one number.
Email/password login requires a verified email. Failed login returns generic invalid_credentials.
Google OAuth uses a signed 10-minute state JWT plus httpOnly nonce cookie.
Password-reset tokens are UUID, 24h TTL, single-use, and cleaned per user. Forgot-password always returns a neutral accepted status after validation.
Login next= open-redirect mitigation via getSafeRedirectPath (must be same-origin path, locale-consistent, not protocol-relative).
Least-privilege catalog: architect / support / admin / system. system is not assignable via BH_*_EMAILS or admin UI. Support cannot assign roles or mutate Architect profile/consent.
Middleware gates /ops/admin and /api/admin/* with admin:ops:access, except support ticket console which is support:ops:access. API handlers also call requirePermission() which loads the live DB role.
Admin account listing excludes password hashes. Support lookup returns safe billing flags only.
.gitignore ignores .env* except .env.example and ignores .data/. .env.example documents secret names without values. No committed sk_live_/whsec_/connection-string values found.
Trace, analytics, support, and Fab 5 live-runner paths redact secret-like strings. Admin responses explicitly omit secrets.
Cron/ops agent routes use timing-safe Bearer compare against CRON_SECRET / IMANI_HEARTBEAT_SECRET.
Stripe webhooks require stripe-signature and constructEvent against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Invalid signatures return 400 without secret leakage.

Auth, login, registration, support, and eligibility forms use server-side validation. Postgres access uses tagged-template parameterization. Analytics ingest allowlists event names and truncates strings.
Launch ops errors record sanitized codes. Consent history is append-only from the support path. Verification/reset URLs are console-logged only when SMTP is missing and NODE_ENV is not production.
Row 20 Founder-accepted least privilege remains: support:ops:access for tickets; dashboards, billing reconcile, and role assign stay admin-only. AI executives are not human credential holders.

findings.title: No brute-force or IP rate limits on login, register, support, or analytics APIs
findings.detail: Login and registration have no attempt lockout. Forgot-password and resend-verification only apply a 60-second per-email cooldown. POST /api/support/request, POST /api/analytics/event, and POST /api/marketing/session have no rate limits. express-rate-limit is a transitive dependency and is not used in app routes.
findings.baselineGap: Row 69 logging/ops hardening implied abuse controls; Row 182 explicitly requires rate-limit review.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Add IP- and account-keyed rate limits on auth, support, and public ingest endpoints. Add login lockout after repeated failures.

findings.title: Architect application MFA is not implemented
findings.detail: Email/password plus optional Google Sign-In are the only Architect auth factors. Row 69 baseline text includes MFA. Vendor MFA is mixed: Google Workspace and Stripe PASS (Row 74/77); Cloudflare 2FA INACTIVE with Founder-accepted residual risk; Vercel and Supabase dashboard MFA remain Founder verification required. This finding is the application-login gap, not a request to change Cloudflare/Vercel/Stripe settings from this row.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Document whether Architect MFA is in-scope for launch or a post-launch control. If in-scope, add TOTP/WebAuthn. Do not treat vendor MFA as covering Architect accounts.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy or other security headers in app config
findings.detail: next.config.ts and vercel.json do not set CSP, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. HSTS may be provided by the Vercel platform but is not codified in the repository. Clickjacking and XSS defense currently rely on React defaults and platform defaults.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Add headers() in next.config.ts (CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors 'self', Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy). Confirm Vercel production HSTS separately without changing DNS.

findings.title: Middleware authorizes pages from JWT role claims that can be stale for 30 days
findings.detail: middleware.ts uses session.role from the signed cookie. requirePermission() on API/server actions reloads the user from the store, so API role changes take effect immediately. Page routes under /ops/admin and /architect remain reachable until the JWT expires or the user re-logins after a demotion. Password reset also does not clear existing bh-session cookies (see F-07).
findings.baselineGap: least privilege enforcement at request time
findings.recommendedRemediation: Include a session version or roleIssuedAt in the JWT and compare against the store in middleware, or shorten TTL and re-issue on role change. Revoke sessions on password reset and role demotion.

findings.title: npm audit reports 11 high and 1 moderate vulnerabilities
findings.detail: Direct packages flagged via transitive chains: next (postcss, sharp/libvips) and puppeteer (@puppeteer/browsers → extract-zip symlink traversal). Other high issues: brace-expansion, fast-uri, js-yaml, nanoid. Moderate: hono (transitive). No criticals. Fixes are reported as available; upgrading puppeteer/next in production is a follow-up engineering change, not part of this review-only deliverable.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Run a dedicated dependency-upgrade branch with npm audit fix, puppeteer upgrade, and regression of Blueprint PDF generation. Do not mix that change into this review PR.

findings.title: Any admin:ops:access principal can resolve Founder decisions and trigger an AOS tick
findings.detail: POST /api/admin/aos/founder-decision requires admin:ops:access then calls resolveFounderDecision and, on APPROVED, runAosTick. Kimberly Walker (human) is the sole Founder acceptance authority. If BH_ADMIN_EMAILS includes any non-Founder mailbox, that admin can record an APPROVED founder decision in software. This is a governance/control finding, not evidence that Founder approval was fabricated in this review.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Bind founder-decision approval to a Founder-only allowlist (not generic admin). Keep Kimberly Walker (AI) excluded.

findings.title: Password reset does not revoke existing sessions
findings.detail: resetPasswordAction updates the password hash and consumes reset tokens but does not expire or rotate bh-session cookies. A stolen session remains valid for the remaining JWT TTL (up to 30 days).
findings.recommendedRemediation: Store a passwordChangedAt / sessionVersion on the user and reject JWTs issued before that timestamp.

findings.title: Development AUTH_SECRET fallback exists
findings.detail: getAuthSecret() returns the literal development-only-auth-secret when AUTH_SECRET is unset and NODE_ENV==='development'. Vercel production sets NODE_ENV=production so this should not apply there. Risk is a mis-set NODE_ENV on a reachable host.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Fail closed whenever VERCEL_ENV is production or preview, regardless of NODE_ENV.

findings.title: Resend-verification enumerates accounts
findings.detail: resendVerificationEmailAction returns not_found for unknown emails and already_verified for verified/Google accounts, unlike forgot-password which always returns accepted.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Return a generic sent/accepted status for unknown and already-verified addresses.

findings.title: A single CRON_SECRET authorizes a wide ops/agent surface
findings.detail: authorizeHeartbeatRequest gates Imani heartbeat, Michelle/Nia cycles, KPI and analytics durability, AOS tick, AOS validate, monitoring run, and support inbound inject/poll. Compromise of that one bearer token is high blast radius. Compare is timing-safe. Routes are not middleware-gated.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Split secrets per agent/route family. Keep values in Vercel env only; do not print them.

findings.title: Row 73 Stripe live-connect POST can return a webhook signing secret
findings.detail: POST /api/ops/stripe-live-connect is production-only and authorized by x-row73-connect vs ROW73_STRIPE_CONNECT_TOKEN, then calls runRow73StripeLiveConnect({ includeWebhookSecret: true, createWebhook: true, createCheckoutSessions: true }). Intended as a bootstrap tool; still a high-privilege secret-exfiltration path if the token leaks.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Disable or Founder-gate this route after bootstrap. Never log the webhook secret. This review did not call the endpoint and did not print secrets.

findings.title: Production Blueprint PDF generation launches Puppeteer with --no-sandbox
findings.detail: Authenticated Architect PDF routes import puppeteer and launch with --no-sandbox --disable-setuid-sandbox, maxDuration 300s. Combined with F-05 this is a DoS and (if RCE exists) container-escape concern. BLUEPRINT_QA_OPEN=1 would also allow print pages to load an arbitrary architectId; .env.example says never enable in production.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Confirm BLUEPRINT_QA_OPEN is unset in Production. Isolate PDF rendering. Upgrade puppeteer.

findings.title: AOS tick logs the full JSON result to the server console
findings.detail: app/api/fab-5/aos/tick/route.ts console.logs { aosTick: true, ...result }. Result objects can include work titles, owner agents, and operational state. Secret redaction is not applied at this log site.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Log counts and IDs only, or pass through redactSecrets() before console.log.

findings.title: Public support form has no max length or IP throttle
findings.detail: validateSupportRequest requires name/email/category/subject and message min length 10, but does not cap message size. Combined with F-01 this is an abuse/storage vector. Support sanitizer redacts card/CVV/password-like substrings before storage.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Cap field lengths and add IP rate limits on /api/support/request.

findings.title: /_internal review pages are Host-header localhost checks only
findings.detail: app/%5Finternal/* pages call assertLocalhostOnly on the Host header and are not session-authenticated. Production hostnames should 404. Risk is Host-header confusion on a misconfigured proxy.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Prefer socket/connection address checks or disable the /_internal tree in production builds.

findings.title: BLUEPRINT_PRINT_SECRET compared with non-timing-safe equality
findings.detail: Print pages compare x-blueprint-print-secret using ===. Low practical risk for a high-entropy header secret.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual after buffering equal-length values, matching heartbeat auth.

findings.title: Auth and support validation is hand-rolled rather than schema-based
findings.detail: zod is a direct dependency but is used primarily in Fab 5 live-agent tool schemas, not auth/support/admin JSON bodies.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Adopt zod (or equivalent) for public and admin JSON/API bodies.

findings.title: GET /api/ops/health is public by design
findings.detail: Returns environment label, service name, and database ok/error/unconfigured. Used by Row 61 monitoring. Low information disclosure; no secrets.

dependencyAudit.notes: Counts only. Advisory titles recorded in F-05. No package payloads, tokens, or lockfile secrets printed.

validation.reason: This deliverable is a review-only status file. No product, marketing, or legal source was changed, so npm run build was not executed. package.json has no typecheck or test script.

recommendedFollowUpWork.title: Add rate limits and login lockout
Revoke sessions on password reset and role change; check live role in middleware
Add security headers (CSP, HSTS, frame-ancestors, nosniff)
Founder-only gate for AOS founder-decision approval
Dependency upgrade branch for npm audit / puppeteer
Decide Architect MFA launch scope vs Row 69 baseline language
